channel.title: Porsche recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne, Panamera and Taycan Rearview Camera Failure
item.description: In these vehicles, the rearview camera image may not show up on the display screen when the vehicle is shifted into reverse. Dealers will fix this by updating the driver assistance software, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne and Panamera fuel pump bolts may leak fuel
item.description: The fasteners holding the high pressure fuel pump in place on these vehicles may not be tightened properly, which can allow fuel to leak. This affects certain Porsche Panamera, Panamera E-Hybrid, and Cayenne vehicles. Porsche is recalling these vehicles so dealers can inspect and tighten the connections, and replace the fuel pump and fuel lines if needed.

item.title: Porsche Panamera Suspension Strut May Loosen
item.description: On the front suspension, a retaining ring that holds the top of the strut in place may come loose over time. If the ring lets go, the strut can become dislodged from its mount, and the strut spring can lose air pressure, affecting how the front suspension holds together.

item.title: Porsche Taycan front passenger airbag may switch off
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain Taycan vehicles because of a fault in the system that decides whether the front passenger airbag should be switched on. This system is meant to sense whether someone is sitting in the front passenger seat. An error in it can turn the front passenger airbag off. Dealers will replace the front passenger seat cushion at no cost, and Porsche has mailed notification letters to owners.

item.title: Porsche Taycan High-Voltage Battery Short Circuit Risk
item.description: On certain Porsche Taycan vehicles, the high-voltage battery that powers the car may develop a short circuit inside one of its battery modules. This recall expands and replaces three earlier Taycan battery recalls, so even vehicles already repaired under those earlier recalls will need to have this new repair completed as well.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Battery Short Circuit Fire Risk
item.description: On these Porsche Taycan vehicles, the high-voltage battery that powers the car may develop a short circuit inside one of its battery modules.

item.title: Porsche Taycan headlight software affects parking lights
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain Taycan cars that may have been built with the wrong software in the module that controls the headlights. Because of that software, the parking lights may not work as intended when the turn signals are switched on. As a result, these cars do not meet the federal rule covering lamps and reflective equipment. Dealers will update the headlight control module software, and there is no charge to the owner for the update.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Control Arm Crack Risk
item.description: The upper control arm on the driver's side front axle may have been installed with cracks. A cracked control arm can break, which can cause a sudden loss of steering and wheel control.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Front Brake Hoses May Leak
item.description: In certain Porsche Taycan vehicles, the front brake hoses can develop cracks and begin to leak brake fluid. Losing brake fluid can weaken how well the brakes work and make it take longer for the vehicle to stop when needed. Dealers will fix the problem by replacing the front brake hoses, free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Battery Short Circuit Fire Risk
item.description: The high-voltage battery in these vehicles may develop a short circuit inside its battery modules. A short circuit like this increases the risk of the battery catching fire.

item.title: Porsche Taycan high-voltage battery may short circuit
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain Taycan models because the high-voltage battery may develop a short circuit within its battery modules.

item.title: Porsche 911 rear seat belt may not hold child seat securely
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain 911 vehicles. The rear seat belts have a locking feature that is meant to hold a child seat firmly in place. On these vehicles that lock can switch off too early, so the child seat may not end up properly secured. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for occupant crash protection. Dealers will look at the rear three-point belts and replace them where needed.

item.title: Porsche portable charging cable and outlet can overheat
item.description: Porsche is recalling a number of electric and plug-in hybrid models, including the Taycan, Cayenne E-Hybrid and Panamera 4S E-Hybrid. When the compact charging system is used with its industrial 220-volt or 240-volt plug at the 100 percent charge setting, some home outlets cannot handle the electrical current the system needs. The outlet or the charging cable can then overheat. Dealers will supply a new 220-volt/240-volt portable charging cable with a built-in temperature sensor, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche Taycan High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: On certain Porsche Taycan and Taycan Turbo S vehicles, along with several other Taycan variants, the high-voltage battery may develop a short circuit inside one of its battery modules. This means an unwanted electrical connection can form somewhere inside the battery pack. When a short circuit like this happens inside the battery, it increases the chances that a fire could start in the vehicle.

item.title: Porsche 911 Seat-Mounted Air Bags May Deploy Unnecessarily
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain 911 models that have the optional full bucket seats installed. These seats include air bags built into them. In some cases, those seat air bags may deploy unnecessarily during a crash, meaning they can go off even when they are not needed. This problem only affects vehicles equipped with the special bucket seat option, not vehicles with standard seats.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Battery Seal Issue Raises Fire Risk
item.description: In these vehicles, the high voltage battery may not have enough sealant applied during manufacturing. Without enough sealant, liquid can get into the battery and build up inside it over time. This buildup of liquid inside the battery can cause electrical arcing. Dealers will test each vehicle's battery for leaks and replace the battery if needed, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Rear Hazard and Parking Lights May Fail
item.description: After a Cayenne is turned off, the rear hazard warning lights and parking lights may fail to come on if they are turned on within 10 seconds after the vehicle's gateway control unit shuts off. Because of this, the vehicle does not meet the federal lighting safety standard for lamps and reflective devices. In this situation, other drivers may not be able to see the hazard or parking lights when they are needed.

item.title: Porsche Rear Seat Belt Anchors May Not Be Tight
item.description: The screw that attaches the lower seat belt anchor to the seat frame on the outboard rear seats may not have been tightened properly. This affects certain Porsche Macan, Macan S, Panamera 4, and Panamera 4 E-Hybrid vehicles, among other Porsche models. Dealers will replace and tighten the lower rear outboard seat belt anchor screws, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche 911 GT3 brake lights may confuse following drivers
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain 911 GT3 Touring cars. A software error in the control unit for the rear spoiler can let two center brake lights come on at the same time — the one on the car and the one on the spoiler — when the spoiler is raised by hand at speeds below 56 mph. Federal rules on vehicle lighting do not allow this. A dealer will reprogram the spoiler control unit.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Brake Wear Warning Shows Wrong Color
item.description: On some Taycan vehicles, the dashboard display that is supposed to warn the driver when the brake pads are worn shows the warning in the wrong color. Because the color of this warning is incorrect, a driver may not recognize it as a signal that the brake pads need attention, since the indicator does not display the way it is meant to.

item.title: Porsche 911 Carrera may be missing body welds
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain 911 Carrera vehicles over a problem that happened when the car bodies were built. Because of an error in the production line process, various welds may be missing from the body of the vehicle. Welds are what join the metal panels and frame pieces together. Dealers will inspect the welds and repair them if needed, at no cost, and Porsche is mailing letters to owners.

item.title: Porsche Taycan passenger seat belt warning does not work
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain Taycan vehicles. When someone is sitting in the passenger seat without the seat belt fastened, the seat belt warning light and the reminder chime do not come on the way they are supposed to. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal government's safety standard covering occupant crash protection. Dealers will update the software in the instrument cluster, the display area behind the steering wheel, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche Panamera Coolant Pump May Spark Electrical Fire
item.description: Certain Porsche Panamera models may have a problem with the external coolant pump used for the climate control system. Moisture can get inside this pump, and when it does, it can cause an electrical short circuit. This kind of short circuit happens when the pump is exposed to humidity it isn't designed to handle, affecting the electrical connection inside it.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Suspension Strut Can Fail
item.description: Certain Porsche Taycan vehicles have a suspension strut with a retaining ring on top that can come loose over time. If the ring loosens, the strut can become dislodged and lose air, affecting the air suspension at that corner of the vehicle.

item.title: Porsche 911 GT3 Seat Belt Anchor Screw Loose
item.description: On some Porsche 911 GT3 vehicles, the screw that attaches the lower seat belt anchor to the seat frame may not have been tightened properly during assembly. Because the screw is not fully tightened, the anchor may not be as securely attached to the seat frame as it should be. This affects how firmly the seat belt anchor stays fixed to the seat frame on the affected vehicles.

item.title: Porsche Macan Missing Headlight Adjustment Screw Caps
item.description: Some Porsche Macan and Macan S vehicles are missing the caps that cover the screws used to adjust the low-beam headlights. Without these caps in place, the headlights on these vehicles could end up improperly adjusted.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Screen And Camera Can Go Black
item.description: On certain 2020-2022 Taycan vehicles, a software error can cause the center screen, including the rearview camera image, and the touch control panel to stay black right after the car is started. The Real-Top-View image, including the rearview camera, can also flicker instead of showing a steady picture.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Seat Wiring May Disable Airbags
item.description: On certain 2020-2021 Porsche Taycan vehicles, the wire harness for the driver or passenger seat may become damaged when the seat is adjusted from side to side. A damaged wire harness in the seat may turn off the air bags for that seat. Dealers will check the seat wire harness for damage, add tape to help hold it in place, and repair any damaged wires.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Rear Seat Belt Blocks Child Seat
item.description: Some Taycan vehicles with the optional rear center seat have a seat belt buckle wiring harness that can block access to the lower anchor points for the right rear seat. This can make it hard to properly attach a child seat in that seat.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Front and Rear Suspension Misaligned
item.description: The front and rear suspension on this Taycan may be misaligned. When the suspension is out of alignment, the tires can wear prematurely or unevenly.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Rear Axle Alignment Missed
item.description: After an earlier recall repair was completed on these vehicles, the rear axle alignment may not have been inspected as it should have been. Skipping that inspection step means the rear axle could be misaligned. A misaligned rear axle can cause the tires to wear unevenly or wear out faster than normal.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Rear Suspension Bolts May Be Loose
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain Taycan vehicles because the screw connections that hold the front and rear upper control arms on the rear axle may be loose. These connections are part of the suspension system that keeps the wheels properly attached and controlled. If a connection isn't tight, it could work its way loose or fail over time. Dealers will replace the affected screw connections to correct the problem.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Hazard Lights May Activate Falsely
item.description: The pre-collision automatic hazard lights on certain Taycan vehicles may turn on during situations that are not actual emergencies. Because the lights are not being used the way they're meant to be, the vehicle does not meet the federal requirements for this equipment.

item.title: Porsche 911 and Taycan Brake Booster Rod Detachment
item.description: Porsche is recalling certain 911 Carrera and Taycan vehicles because a rod connection in the brake booster may be loose. The rod could come loose and detach completely. If it detaches, the brake pedal can fail, and a failed brake pedal raises the risk of a crash.

item.title: Porsche seat belts may not lock child car seats properly
item.description: On some Porsche cars, including the Panamera, Taycan and 911, the seat belts have a locking feature used to hold a child seat in place. That lock can switch off too soon, so the belt may not hold the child restraint securely. Because of this, the cars do not meet a federal safety standard covering occupant protection in a crash. Dealers will check the seat belt assemblies and replace them if needed at no cost.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Steering Column May Detach
item.description: Porsche says the screw connecting the steering column to the steering box on some Cayenne SUVs may fail. If it does, the steering column can become detached from the steering box, affecting the driver's ability to steer the vehicle.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Software Fault Can Cut Power
item.description: A software problem in the monitoring system can wrongly detect a fault and shut down the powertrain, causing the car to suddenly lose the power that drives it. Dealers will reprogram the power electronics and the engine control unit to fix this, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche Panamera and Taycan: Front Suspension Arm Defect
item.description: The front lower trailing arms on these vehicles were not manufactured correctly and may break. Dealers will replace the front lower trailing arms with correctly made parts, free of charge.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Engine Cylinder Cracks Can Stall Car
item.description: Some Cayenne GTS vehicles have an engine problem where cracks can develop on the surface inside the engine cylinder. Over time, these cracks may cause damage to the engine, which could make the engine stall while you are driving, or cause the engine to develop an oil leak. Porsche dealers will replace the entire engine completely, free of charge, to fix the issue with these vehicles.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne Passenger Airbag May Not Deploy
item.description: On certain Porsche Cayenne, Cayenne Coupe, Cayenne S Coupe, Cayenne GTS, Cayenne GTS Coupe, and Cayenne E-Hybrid Coupe vehicles, a heating element that should have been installed in the front passenger seat back was left out. This part affects the system that senses whether a passenger is sitting in the seat, which can throw off its readings. Because of this, the front passenger airbag may fail to deploy.
